key_insight: A zero-shot, agentic LLM workflow can extract key lung resection pathology fields from narrative reports with high recall, approaching a supervised baseline.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce manual chart abstraction for cancer staging and tumor registry workflows, especially where annotated training data is scarce.
method: Compared a zero-shot agentic workflow using five open-source generative LLMs.
Targeted 13 College of American Pathologists synoptic fields from lung resection pathology reports.
Benchmarked against a supervised GatorTron NER-RE system using a registry-aligned evaluation.
evidence_signal: The supervised baseline reached Micro-F1 0.960, while the best zero-shot model (GPT-OSS-20B) reached Micro-F1 0.893 with recall 0.949, including complex relation extraction such as pathologic stage.
watch_item: Performance was lower than the supervised baseline, so real-world deployment still needs careful validation for accuracy, consistency, and edge cases.
paper_title: Prompt, Plan, Extract: Zero-Shot Agentic LLMs Workflows for Lung Pathology Extraction from Clinical Narratives
